challenge: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 · Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data

production.frontend_host: Vercel (static React/Vite, deployed automatically from main)
production.api_proxy: Vercel rewrites /api/* to the Render API

features: Three steps: outline a field, record crops by zone, get a zone plan
Comparison of 3 rotation strategies (S0 current, S1 Water, S2 Soil) with why, evidence, benefits, gaps and risks
Printable A4 plan: zone sketch with areas, zone advice and the 3-strategy comparison
NASA HLS monthly vegetation history of the Barranca study field (observed, months without data are not filled)
Crop water from FAO-56 Kc x NASA POWER ET0 (calculated, relative)
Small reproducible seasonal model (44 NASA HLS observations, one study field) — proof of concept

evidence_types.observed: NASA HLS v2.0 satellite NDVI (30 m), GPM IMERG upper-basin rain
evidence_types.declared: crops and sowing months entered by the farmer
evidence_types.calculated: FAO-56 crop water with NASA POWER ET0; areas with Shapely/pyproj
evidence_types.agronomic_rules: DRA Lima / MIDAGRI sowing calendar, crop families, legumes
evidence_types.model_inference: seasonal low-vegetation probability, only for the exact Barranca study polygon

ai_model_label: Small reproducible seasonal model (44 NASA HLS observations, one study field) — proof of concept
ai_model_training: 33 chronological HLS observations for holdout evaluation; production fit on all 44
notes: Relative comparisons for discussion with a technician. No yields, profits, water savings or field validation are claimed. Fields outside Barranca receive guidance from general rules only.
